{{Quote|Last time I gamble with a ''Cragmoloid''&hellip;|Lando Calrissian|<ref name="UYV" />}}
'''Cragmoloids''' were a rare [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of intimidating [[pachydermoid]]s with massive builds. They had big, flat [[Ear/Legends|ears]], manipulative [[Nose/Legends|trunks]] and a number of [[Tooth/Legends|tusks]] that could be used in combat&mdash;and that were valued by [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]]. They also had less pachydermoid traits, including [[Limb/Legends|hands]] with five nailed fingers. Although prone to attacking in a rage, particularly when facing subterfuge, Cragmoloids disliked gratuitous violence and were a proud, peaceful people. Cragmoloids loved their families and tended to get depressed if separated from them.

Cragmoloids evolved on the rocky [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ankus/Legends|Ankus]], where they were [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and forced to allow the planet to be [[Mining/Legends|strip-mined]] by a corporation called [[Tagge Company/Legends|TaggeCo]]. Cragmoloids also suffered frequent attacks by hunters who sought their valuable ivory, a peril that prompted many Cragmoloids to the humiliation of simply sawing their own tusks off. A small number of Cragmoloids left their world to earn a living among the [[Star/Legends|stars]]; some of these were [[Boulad]], an [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] living on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]; and [[Rooty]], a [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]] and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] operating in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|For one of the feeble trunkless, you are a pleasant exception.|Boulad, to Gregar Typho|<ref name="CN">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref>}}
Cragmoloids were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[pachydermoid]]s that resembled [[Humanoid/Legends|anthropomorphic]] [[Elephant/Legends|elephants]],<ref name="UAA" /> or simply elephants walking on their hind [[Limb/Legends|legs]].<ref name="AMA">{{LivingForce|A Mon Alone}}</ref> Cragmoloids had stiff,<ref name="US" /> thick, leathery skin that protected them from damage, and two elephantine, flap-like [[Ear/Legends|ears]].<ref name="UAA" /> Among the folds of their skin,<ref name="AMA" /> a Cragmoloid had two sharp, small, [[red]], beady [[Eye/Legends|eyes]],<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="AMA" /> which opened wide when the individual was surprised.<ref name="CN" /> When crying, each of the eyes shed half a [[Liter/Legends|liter]] of [[Water/Legends|water]] as a tear.<ref name="AMA" />

Another pachydermoid trait was the thick facial [[Nose/Legends|trunk]],<ref name="US" /> which was a manipulative organ: Cragmoloids used their trunk to frisk individuals. They also raised it in moments of surprise.<ref name="CN" /> While some Cragmoloids had only one trunk,<ref name="UYV" /> others had two smaller, secondary trunks surrounding the main one. Cragmoloids had natural [[Tooth/Legends|tusks]] under the trunk. These could be used in combat to impale an opponent or during a wrath-driven charge.<ref name="UAA" /> Some Cragmoloids had two big tusks,<ref name="UYV" /> while others had four smaller ones.<ref name="UAA" /> In any case, the tusks could be, and sometimes were, sawed off.<ref name="US" />

Cragmoloids were massive in size, commonly reaching three [[Meter/Legends|meters]] of height,<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="AMA" /> and weighing over two hundred [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] in adulthood.<ref name="US" /> Not only big, but also very strong, cumbersome and intimidating, they commonly found that hiding their bulk was a difficult task.<ref name="UAA" /> Other Cragmoloid physical traits were less pachydermoid. The top of the head presented coarse, stringy hair,<ref name="US" /> at least in some cases. While Cragmoloids had three-toed, clawed feet,<ref name="UAA" /> their massive five-fingered<ref name="UYV" /> hands were humanoid in shape<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="UYV" /> and had nails.<ref name="UYV" />

Cragmoloids began their adolescence at eight [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of age, reaching biological maturity at fifteen. They typically suffered no ills of age before reaching forty, and were considered to be old only at eighty-seven. A Cragmoloid could easily reach the advanced age of one hundred and twenty years.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|I would hear more of your excellent family.|Boulad|<ref name="CN" />}}
[[File:Rootylando1.png|thumb|left|Cragmoloids disliked duplicity]]
The Cragmoloid people were proud<ref name="UAA" /> and valued a promise as a bond.<ref name="CN" /> They considered that losing one's tusks was a severe humiliation. They also preferred to face setbacks with direct answers instead of what they considered to be dishonorable tricks<ref name="UAA" />&mdash;something that did not stop them from pursuing careers in organized crime.<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="CN" /> Duplicity and deception commonly exasperated Cragmoloids, who were prone to violent attacks of rage when angered. Notwithstanding their physical prowess, Cragmoloids believed that unjustified violence was barbaric and to be avoided.<ref name="UAA" />

Their civilization was organized into clans. Cragmoloids were so close to their families that they suffered severe depressions if separated from their homes or their friends.<ref name="UAA" /> A Cragmoloid always preferred chatting about kinship to talking about any other subject, and they commonly praised their direct relatives. [[Alien/Legends|Aliens]] speaking with a Cragmoloid sometimes resorted to asking about their families to obtain the Cragmoloid's trust&mdash;although only after enduring many minutes of speeches.<ref name="CN" /> Cragmoloids had one-word names. Representative appellations included Akoom, Darak, Ormoj, Urun, Vuula,<ref name="UAA" /> Bachus, Ganesh and Trusk.<ref name="US" />

Cragmoloids were an isolated people, commonly speaking only [[Cragii]], the native [[Language/Legends|language]] of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="US" /> Cragmoloids traveling to other [[Planet/Legends|planets]] commonly learned to speak, but not to read, [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]].<ref name="UAA" /> Non-verbal aspects of Cragii was not a widely-known subject on other worlds: a grunt could be construed to mean either acknowledgment, amusement or digestive upset.<ref name="CN" />

==History==
{{Quote|I'm looking for the Cragmoloid Boulad.|Gregar Typho|<ref name="CN" />}}
The Cragmoloids evolved on the plains of [[Ankus/Legends|Ankus]], a rocky planet<ref name="UAA" /> in one of the [[Freestanding subsectors/Legends|freestanding subsectors]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="atlas">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> At some point prior to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Cragmoloids joined the [[galactic community]]. Although a number of Cragmoloids were identified as [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]], none of them became a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]].<ref name="UAA" /> The Cragmoloids also became prey to professional [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]], who [[Death/Legends|killed]] the pachydermoids to keep the ivory from the Cragmoloids' valuable tusks. That was not the species' only off-world threat:<ref name="US" /> the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], created in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] all the available Cragmoloids, and the [[Company/Legends|company]] [[Tagge Company/Legends|TaggeCo]] performed extensive [[Mining/Legends|mining]] on Ankus. These three factors pushed the Cragmoloid species towards extinction.<ref name="US" /> As the Empire had caused some of their worries, a few Cragmoloids joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], hoping to help their kin.<ref name="UAA" />

==Cragmoloids in the galaxy==
{{Quote|And if you know the people of Ankus, you know that we do not bargain in such things. Our word is our bond.|Boulad|<ref name="CN" />}}
Cragmoloids were rarely seen in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="UAA" /> partly as they needed to adapt common appliances to their massive bulks. [[Boulad]], a Cragmoloid [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] in the [[Undercity (Taris)|Undercity]] of the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], hollowed out a [[resiplex]] to create a dwelling appropriate for his size. Circa 18 BBY, Boulad sold the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Security guard/Legends|security guard]] [[Gregar Typho/Legends|Gregar Typho]] valuable information about the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious's]] presence on the planet [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]].<ref name="CN" />

At some point prior to [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="20 BBY">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign is set one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As the ''Living Force'' adventure ''[[Below the Belt: Philology|Philology]]'' [[Cularin's disappearance|moved]] the campaign forward ten years to the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and the adventure ''[[Night Eyes: Night's Homecoming|Night's Homecoming]]'' established that by Year 4 of the campaign over a year had elapsed since the events of ''Philology'', ''[[A Mon Alone]]'' can therefore be dated to circa [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]].</ref> two three-meter tall Cragmoloids, [[Noba]] and [[Ook]], were captured on Ankus by the [[Chevin/Legends|Chevin]] [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adept]] [[Phylus Mon]]. Mon [[Prison/Legends|jailed]] the Cragmoloids in his menagerie, the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[Animiasma]]'', along with other uncommonly seen non-Humans. Although the Cragmoloids were intimidating even behind bars, they were really very depressed over their situation.<ref name="AMA" />

Most Cragmoloids were unable to escape from Ankus to the [[Star/Legends|stars]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Those who could commonly decided to saw off their own tusks to avoid the threat of hunters, but to many that was an unbearable humiliation. The free Cragmoloids worked as [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] or with [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]],<ref name="US" /> but the species was almost exclusively seen in Imperial work camps.<ref name="UAA" />

Around [[10 BBY/Legends|10 BBY]], the Cragmoloid [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] and [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]] [[Rooty]] reached the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. Ashamed for having turned his massive back to his planet, Rooty hoped to forget his disgrace in a hedonistic search of pleasure and rubbing shoulders with the likes of the Human smugglers [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Salla Zend]] and [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]. In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], Rooty defeated Calrissian at the card game [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]], winning the 20,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] bet that the [[Socorran]] had placed on his hand. Calrissian then admitted he had bet more [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] than he actually had available, and offered an alternative payment to Rooty. Understanding that Calrissian was trying to cheat him, the Cragmoloid was enraged and physically threatened Calrissian. A certain [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|bystander]] offered to pay Rooty the remainder of the debt and, although Rooty agreed, he still retained a dislike for Calrissian in later [[Time/Legends|times]].<ref name="US" /><ref name="UYV" />

During the Galactic Civil War, the Cragmoloid [[Bouncer (occupation)/Legends|bouncer]] [[Dimbu]] worked at the speakeasy [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] [[Chorba Chuggers]]. With a prohibition on [[Alcohol/Legends|alcohol]] in place on the planet [[Kinyen/Legends|Kinyen]], Dimbu ensured no law enforcement officers were able to enter the establishment.<ref name="Strongholds">''[[Strongholds of Resistance]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Cragmoloids first appeared in the [[2000]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika 1|''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika'' 1]], written by [[Mike Kennedy]] and drawn by [[Carlos Meglia]]. The background for the species was expanded in [[Andrew Hind]]'s article ''[[Unusual Suspects]]'', published in [[2001]] in [[Star Wars Gamer 6|''Star Wars Gamer'' 6]], and again in [[2003]]'s ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''. In [[2008]], the species received an entry in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.

[[File:Bestbirthdayevercragmoloid.png|thumb|right|From ''Best Birthday Ever'']]
Although ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' repeats a number of sentences from ''Unusual Suspects,'' it also introduces a number of inconsistencies, mostly in terms of role-playing game rules: The ''Gamer'' article considers the Cragmoloids to be larger in game terms, and adds a bonus to their perception and a penalization to their charisma to reflect their cumbersomeness and intimidating appearance. Both sources recognize that the Cragmoloids can attack with tusks or by ramming, but each source uses different rules for the effects. ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' also provides a table for the Cragmoloid lifespan, while ''Unusual Suspects'' suggests that the lifespan of a Cragmoloid equals a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee's]]. In this last case, this article follows the ''Anthology'' lifespan table, because it is the more recent source.

[[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion]] places the Cragmoloid home planet Ankus in the Mid Rim. Previous sources located it in the limits<ref name="US" /> of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], near [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]].<ref name="UAA" /> Ankus shares its name with an implement used to handle elephants.<ref name="NationalGeographicAfricanElephant">{{WebCite|url=http://www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/mammals/a/african-elephant|text=African Elephant|archivedate=20170912184736}}</ref>

Huge, pachydermoid aliens that shares physical traits in common with the Cragmoloids appears in two comedic, non-[[canon]] stories. In "[[Best Birthday Ever]]", first published in [[Star Wars Tales 16|''Star Wars Tales'' 16]] in 2003, a pachydermoid appears waiting in a queue with the Twi'lek [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]] [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]].<ref name="BBE">{{Tales|16|Best Birthday Ever}}</ref> Another story, "[[Fett Club (comic story)|Fett Club]]," first published in [[Star Wars Tales 24|''Star Wars Tales'' 24]] in [[2005]], features a pink, tusked elephantine humanoid who answers a fake advertisement to become a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]]. In actuality, the ad is a trick by [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]], [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], to find a template for his [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]]. The pink pachydermoid escapes the audition.<ref name="FC">{{Tales|24|Fett Club (comic story)}}</ref>
